nodes.name: Webhook: Look up contact by email

parameters.query:
-- ALWAYS RETURNS EXACTLY ONE ROW, even on a miss.
--
-- A plain `select ... where email = $1` returns nothing when the contact is unknown, and an n8n
-- node with no input items does not run — so the "not found" branch would never fire and the
-- webhook would hang with no response. The left join against a one-row subquery makes the miss an
-- explicit `found = false` instead of an absence.
select
  q.e                                   as email_in,
  (c.hs_object_id is not null)          as found,
  c.hs_object_id,
  c.email,
  c.firstname,
  c.lastname,
  c.company,
  c.state,
  c.lifecyclestage,
  c.hs_lastmodifieddate,
  c.synced_at
from (select $1::text as e) q
left join hubspot.hubspot_contacts c
       on lower(c.email) = q.e;

insert into hubspot.hubspot_contacts
select * from jsonb_populate_recordset(null::hubspot.hubspot_contacts, $1::jsonb)
on conflict (hs_object_id) do update set
  email = excluded.email,
  firstname = excluded.firstname,
  lastname = excluded.lastname,
  company = excluded.company,
  state = excluded.state,
  lifecyclestage = excluded.lifecyclestage,
  hs_lastmodifieddate = excluded.hs_lastmodifieddate,
  synced_at = excluded.synced_at

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ found: false, source: 'hubspot', email: $json.email_in, reason: 'No HubSpot contact has this email address.' }) }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ inputs: [{ id: String($('Contact to enrich').first().json.contact_id) }] }) }}

parameters.query:
insert into hubspot.hubspot_companies as t
select * from jsonb_populate_recordset(null::hubspot.hubspot_companies, $1::jsonb)
on conflict (hs_object_id) do update set
  name = excluded.name,
  domain = excluded.domain,
  state = excluded.state,
  lifecyclestage = excluded.lifecyclestage,
  -- MERGED, NOT REPLACED. This path knows only the ONE contact that was just looked up, so
  -- assigning excluded.associated_contact_ids would erase every other contact a previous
  -- lookup had cached on this row. The full sync may replace the array outright — it reads the
  -- complete set from HubSpot — but an on-demand lookup only ever adds to it.
  associated_contact_ids = (
    select coalesce(array_agg(distinct x), '{}'::bigint[])
      from unnest(t.associated_contact_ids || excluded.associated_contact_ids) as x
  ),
  hs_lastmodifieddate = excluded.hs_lastmodifieddate,
  synced_at = excluded.synced_at

insert into hubspot.hubspot_deals as t
select * from jsonb_populate_recordset(null::hubspot.hubspot_deals, $1::jsonb)
on conflict (hs_object_id) do update set
  dealname = excluded.dealname,
  pipeline = excluded.pipeline,
  dealstage = excluded.dealstage,
  amount = excluded.amount,
  closedate = excluded.closedate,
  -- MERGED, NOT REPLACED. This path knows only the ONE contact that was just looked up, so
  -- assigning excluded.associated_contact_ids would erase every other contact a previous
  -- lookup had cached on this row. The full sync may replace the array outright — it reads the
  -- complete set from HubSpot — but an on-demand lookup only ever adds to it.
  associated_contact_ids = (
    select coalesce(array_agg(distinct x), '{}'::bigint[])
      from unnest(t.associated_contact_ids || excluded.associated_contact_ids) as x
  ),
  associated_company_ids = (
    select coalesce(array_agg(distinct x), '{}'::bigint[])
      from unnest(t.associated_company_ids || excluded.associated_company_ids) as x
  ),
  hs_lastmodifieddate = excluded.hs_lastmodifieddate,
  synced_at = excluded.synced_at

-- ALWAYS RETURNS EXACTLY ONE ROW, even when nothing resolves — the same reason the mirror lookup
-- above is written this way. A bare select returns no rows for a contact with no deal and no
-- company, an n8n node with no input items does not run, and the response node would never be
-- reached: the caller would get HTTP 200, an empty body, and no way to tell a miss from a hang.
-- The lateral join against a one-row subquery makes "no deal" an explicit null instead of an
-- absence.
--
-- ONE implementation of the fallback chain, in migration 065, called rather than reimplemented in
-- JavaScript: the contact own deals first, newest hs_lastmodifieddate winning, and only then the
-- deals of the contact companies. deal_via says which branch answered, because "their deal" and
-- "a deal at their club" are different claims.
--
-- Read back from the database rather than from the rows just written, deliberately: the company
-- fallback can draw on deals cached by earlier lookups or by the scheduled sync, which this
-- request never saw.
select q.e            as email_in,
       r.hs_object_id as contact_id,
       r.company_ids,
       r.deal_id,
       r.deal_via
  from (select $1::text as e) q
  left join lateral (select * from public.hubspot_deal_for_emails(array[q.e])) r on true;

insert into hubspot.hubspot_deal_stages
select * from jsonb_populate_recordset(null::hubspot.hubspot_deal_stages, $1::jsonb)
on conflict (stage_id) do update set
  pipeline_id = excluded.pipeline_id,
  pipeline_label = excluded.pipeline_label,
  stage_label = excluded.stage_label,
  display_order = excluded.display_order,
  is_closed = excluded.is_closed,
  probability = excluded.probability,
  synced_at = excluded.synced_at
